analysis: The energy option has substantive Earth science, ecology, water systems, climate science, resource recovery, renewable energy and governance. Dynamic Earth moves to its available fall 2028 slot and Research in a Sustainable Delta moves to fall 2026, the only offering. The early applied course introduces research design with a stakeholder, before formal statistics in spring. Energy & Sustainability replaces a second broad statistics course so energy assessment is supported directly. Mathematical Methods, Research Methods & Statistics, Data Science and Econometrics maintain quantitative continuity.

The politics option uses political philosophy and rights, comparative politics, international relations, governance and conflict, plus macroeconomic and public economics methods. Historical and communications courses provide context for institutions and public argument.

The health option introduces brain and behaviour in the first term, then studies social psychology, epidemiology and health psychology. Medical & Health Psychology in fall 2028 replaces the unavailable Introduction to Economics, and its Brain & Behavior prerequisite replaces the history survey on empire. Culture and inequality are covered through sociology, media and race, Native American histories and rights, supported by qualitative methods and statistical research.

Partial alignments include comparative and international politics, introductory economics, social psychology, epidemiology, statistical methods and qualitative research. Introductory Data Science overlaps the interdisciplinary computing component through data manipulation and visualisation. Generic elective slots do not warrant course-level pairings. Research in a Sustainable Delta has relevant stakeholder research, with narrower scope than the required Living Lab. A course research paper is separate from a degree thesis and portfolio.

schedules.label: Energy, ecology & climate
schedules.concept: Studies climate and energy transitions through environmental science, biodiversity, water and material resources. Combines field and data methods with economics and sustainability governance.

schedules.label: Politics, philosophy & economics
schedules.concept: A governance-centred route addressing global inequality, institutions, international law, ethical responsibility, conflict and political economy through political science, philosophy, law, economics and social research.

schedules.label: Culture, psychology & global health
schedules.concept: Studies how behaviour, culture and inequality shape health. Connects social and health psychology with epidemiology, qualitative research and the study of institutions, media and environmental justice.

BENECON312.contribution: Econometrics contributes relevant disciplinary knowledge or methods to the selected GRL direction while remaining a UCR liberal-arts course rather than a direct reproduction of the Groningen component.
BENECON312.topics: Econometrics supplies tools to analyze data to answer questions of causality and prediction. In this course you learn three estimators—Ordinary Least Squares, Generalized Least Squares, and Instrumental Variables—and three tests—t-test, F-test, and LM-test. Understanding the basic rules of econometrics, particularly the sampling distribution concept, is key, and the course uses Monte Carlo simulations in Stata to visualize it. Tools are applied to estimate economic relationships and make predictions, and students write an empirical paper.

ENSDELT312.name: Governance of Sustainability
ENSDELT312.text: This course examines sustainability through the lens of governance: “a process of rule-making and collective decision-making that includes both governmental and non-governmental actors in shaping public policy” (Fenger & Bekkers, 2016). Taking this lens, we ask questions such as how are sustainability policies on the local, national, and international level made and enforced? Which actors represent which interests, and which are most influential? How is public opinion on sustainability shaped, and how does public opinion shape politics? What, at the end of the day, determines effective policy for sustainability? By the end of this course, you will have gained a deep appreciation of the complexity of the governance dimension of sustainability, and have developed the theoretical and practical understanding to critically assess mainstream policy decisions.
